messages.subject: Problem with a matrix product
messages.body_plain:
Hello Nimble Users and Perry,

My model is now checking and compiling correctly, thanks to your advice.

However, I am having difficulties to fit a more complex model. This model extension requires a matrix multiplication with
Z[1:n_obs] <- K[1:n_obs, 1:n_grid] * X[1:n_grid]

To simulate my data in R, I just simply do
Z <- K%*%X

In OpenBUGS, I used the inprod function within a loop :

For (s in 1:n_obs){
 Z[s] <-  inprod(K[s, 1:n_grid], X[1:n_grid])
}

But I didn’t find how to use the inprod function or the %*% product within Nimble. I keep getting errors.

I tried several combinations of index or the asRow(x) function, but without success.

In the majority of my attempts, I have an error message as follow: Error Failed to create the shared library. Followed by a long warning message.

Do you have suggestion, to perform this product?

I attached an R code with my data and Nimble model.

Many thanks,

Jean-Baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Problem with a matrix product
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jean-Baptiste,

Thanks for this case.

It appears there is a bug in our C++ code-generation for inprod.  I’ll file an issue on that but I can’t give you an immediate fix.

I can suggest two alternatives:

1. a slight hand-coding of inprod:  Z[s] <- sum(K[s, 1:n_grid] * X[1:n_grid]).  This worked for me.

2.  The matrix multiplication worked for me.  The version in your code file was this
  Z[1:n_obs] <-  K[,] %*% X[1:n_grid]
That does not necessarily work in BUGS code unless dimensions of K are determined or provided.  But I tried it as you gave it in your message:

Z[1:n_obs] <- K[1:n_obs, 1:n_grid] * X[1:n_grid]

and that worked fine.

If that is also how you tried it and it did not work, can you please send more information?

Note that the two options may have different implications for efficiency.  In the first, each Z[s] is a separate node, which depends on the vectors K[s, 1:n_grid] and X[1:n_grid].  In the second, Z[1:n_obs] is a single vector node, which depends on all of K[,] and X[].  In your case, dimensions of X and subject to updating, while K is constant, so the matrix version may be better.  In a situation where just one element of K  (or elements of one row of K) is being sampled, then it can sometimes be better if only the relevant element of Z needs to be computed.

Perry
